proof_route: A finite family of real lower and upper bounds has an actual common real witness when all cross bounds are consistent, including empty sides.
Proves genuine scalar Fourier-Motzkin elimination for finite inequalities a_i*x+d_i<=0: zero-slope constraints and each negative-positive slope pair characterize existence.

Inducts over finitely many eliminated real coordinates. New constraints are indexed by I sum (I product I), preserving finiteness; coefficient/sign tests deactivate irrelevant rows. Parameter offsets remain continuous, so the projected set is a finite intersection of closed inequalities.
Chooses a finite basis of E. Adds two inequalities encoding objective equality c(u)+a=r. Eliminating all input coordinates derives closedness of the objective image.

Uses the actual EReal supremum of the objective image. It rules out empty U. If the real image is bounded above, its real supremum is in the proved-closed image, and the EReal supremum inequality makes that attained value nonnegative. If unbounded, absence of a nonnegative input would bound the image above by0, a contradiction.
scope: Arbitrary finite-dimensional real normed input space E, any n:Nat, linear inequality functionals A_i:E→linear real with bounds b_i, U={u | forall i:Fin n,A_i(u)<=b_i}, arbitrary affine objective c(u)+a. Assumption 0 <= sSup ((u→EReal(c(u)+a)) image U) entails exists u satisfying every input constraint and c(u)+a>=0. U need not be bounded or supplied nonempty. Closed objective-image membership and attainment are derived, not assumed. No finite-generator representation, Minkowski-Weyl theorem, or conclusion hypothesis is used.
